findings.description: The bucket does not define a server_side_encryption_configuration block, meaning objects are stored without enforced encryption at rest.

findings.issue_category: no public access block / no ACL restriction
findings.description: No ACL is specified and no public access block is configured, leaving the bucket potentially subject to default or overly permissive access settings.
The bucket stores financial ledger export data but has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving sensitive data unencrypted at rest.

Versioning is not enabled on this sensitive ledger data bucket, though this is more of a data integrity concern tied to accidental overwrite/deletion protection relevant to security posture (retained since it affects ability to recover from unauthorized modification).
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, so stored model artifacts are not encrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, leaving operational runbook data (which may contain sensitive operational details) unencrypted at rest.

The ACL value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid canned S3 ACL; if this typo actually resolves to a permissive setting such as log-delivery-write or fails closed to a more permissive default, it can unintentionally grant broader write/read access than intended to the audit trail bucket, which is especially risky for an audit log store.
force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contents to be deleted without additional protection, increasing risk of accidental or malicious data loss for archived reports.

findings.issue_category: unencrypted object upload / plaintext sensitive data
findings.description: The uploaded object is placed into a bucket without server-side encryption enforced and without specifying server_side_encryption on the object itself, so a vendor roster file (potentially containing sensitive vendor/PII data) is stored in plaintext.
